turns.question: Where are routes registered, and how are incoming requests matched to handlers?
turns.text:
I now have enough to answer fully.

## Route registration

- **`routergroup.go`** — `RouterGroup` (embedded in `Engine`) exposes the public API: `GET`, `POST`, `PUT`, `DELETE`, `PATCH`, `HEAD`, `OPTIONS`, `Any`, `Match`, and the generic `Handle(method, path, ...HandlerFunc)`. Each of these shortcut methods calls the unexported `(group *RouterGroup) handle(httpMethod, relativePath string, handlers HandlersChain)` (routergroup.go).
  - `handle()` computes the full path via `calculateAbsolutePath` (joins group's `basePath` with the relative path, `path.go`), merges group + route middleware via `combineHandlers`, then calls **`group.engine.addRoute(httpMethod, absolutePath, handlers)`**.
  - `Group(relativePath, ...HandlerFunc)` creates a child `*RouterGroup` that shares the same `engine` pointer and inherited `Handlers`, which is how nested route groups work.
  - Static file routes (`Static`, `StaticFS`, `StaticFile`) are just sugar that registers `GET`/`HEAD` handlers pointing at `http.FileServer`/`c.File`.

- **`gin.go`** — `(engine *Engine) addRoute(method, path string, handlers HandlersChain)` is where registration actually lands:
  - Looks up (or creates) a `*node` root for the HTTP method in `engine.trees` (a `methodTrees`, i.e. one radix tree per method).
  - Calls `root.addRoute(path, handlers)` (defined in `tree.go`) to insert the path into that method's radix tree.
  - Tracks `engine.maxParams` / `engine.maxSections` for context/pool preallocation.

## Request matching

- **`tree.go`** implements a compressed radix (trie) tree per HTTP method, ported from `julienschmidt/httprouter`:
  - `type node struct{ path, indices string; wildChild bool; nType nodeType; children []*node; handlers HandlersChain; fullPath string }`
  - `node.addRoute` / `node.insertChild` build the tree, splitting/merging edges on longest common prefix, with special handling for `:param` (`param` nodeType) and `*catchAll` (`catchAll` nodeType) segments (`findWildcard`).
  - `node.getValue(path string, params *Params, skippedNodes *[]skippedNode, unescape bool) nodeValue` is the actual matcher: walks the tree byte-by-byte matching the static prefix, follows `indices` for static children, falls back to the wildcard child (`wildChild`) for `:param`/`*catchAll` segments, extracts param values into `Params`, and computes a trailing-slash-redirect (`tsr`) recommendation when no exact match is found. `skippedNodes` supports backtracking when a static-vs-wildcard choice turns out wrong.

- **`gin.go`** ties it together in `(engine *Engine) handleHTTPRequest(c *Context)`, invoked from `ServeHTTP`:
  1. Reads `httpMethod := c.Request.Method` and `rPath := c.Request.URL.Path` (with `UseRawPath`/`UseEscapedPath`/`RemoveExtraSlash` options adjusting `rPath`).
  2. Iterates `engine.trees` for the entry whose `.method == httpMethod`, then calls `root.getValue(rPath, c.params, c.skippedNodes, unescape)`.
  3. On match (`value.handlers != nil`): sets `c.handlers`, `c.Params`, `c.fullPath`, then runs the middleware/handler chain via `c.Next()`.
  4. On no match: if `value.tsr` and `RedirectTrailingSlash` is enabled, redirects; else if `RedirectFixedPath`, tries `findCaseInsensitivePath`; else if `HandleMethodNotAllowed`, checks other method trees for a match and returns 405; otherwise falls through to `engine.allNoRoute` (404).
  - `Engine.ServeHTTP(w http.ResponseWriter, req *http.Request)` is the `http.Handler` entry point — gets a pooled `*Context`, resets it, and calls `handleHTTPRequest`.

## Not verified

- Did not check `context.go` (`c.Next()` / middleware execution loop details) or `path.go` (`cleanPath`/`joinPaths` internals) line-by-line — referenced them by name from imports/usage only.
- Did not run/build the code or execute tests; all conclusions are from static reading of source via `ghx read`.
- Did not check `ginS/` (the global "default engine" shim package) — likely just delegates to a package-level `Engine`, but unconfirmed.

turns.question: How are route parameters like :name captured during tree matching?
turns.text:
Route parameters are captured entirely within `tree.go`, during both tree construction and lookup.

## 1. Recognizing `:name` at insert time

`insertChild(path, fullPath string, handlers HandlersChain)` (tree.go) scans the path with `findWildcard(path string) (wildcard string, i int, valid bool)`:
- It looks for the first `:` or `*` byte not preceded by an escape (`\:`).
- It then scans forward from there until the next `/` or end-of-string, so `wildcard` is the whole segment, e.g. `:name`.
- If `wildcard[0] == ':'`, a new `node{ nType: param, path: wildcard, fullPath: fullPath }` is created and added as a child (`n.addChild(child)`), and `n.wildChild = true` is set on the parent. Per `node.addChild`, a wildcard child is always kept as the **last** entry in `children`, since a node can have at most one param/catch-all child alongside any number of static children.
- If there's more path after `:name` (e.g. `:name/edit`), insertion continues recursively into a new child node for the remainder.
- The node's `path` field literally stores the string `:name` (including the colon) — the colon is what marks it as a param node when read back later (e.g. `n.path[1:]` strips it to get just `name`).

## 2. Capturing the value at match time

In `node.getValue(path string, params *Params, skippedNodes *[]skippedNode, unescape bool)` (tree.go), once the walk reaches a node with `wildChild == true` and no static-index match for the next byte, it falls to:

```go
n = n.children[len(n.children)-1]   // the wildcard child, always last
globalParamsCount++

switch n.nType {
case param:
    end := 0
    for end < len(path) && path[end] != '/' {
        end++
    }
    // path[:end] is the captured value, up to the next '/'
    ...
    (*value.params)[i] = Param{
        Key:   n.path[1:],   // strip leading ':' → "name"
        Value: val,
    }
```

Key details:
- The captured segment is bounded by the next `/` or end of string — params match exactly one path segment, never spanning `/`.
- `val := path[:end]`; if `unescape` is true (driven by `Engine.UnescapePathValues`/`UseRawPath`/`UseEscapedPath`), it's run through `url.QueryUnescape`.
- The `Param{Key: n.path[1:], Value: val}` is appended into `*value.params`, which is preallocated up front to `globalParamsCount` capacity (itself bounded by `Engine.maxParams`, computed once at `addRoute` time via `countParams` in `gin.go`/`tree.go`) — this avoids reallocation per request.
- If there's remaining path after the captured segment (`end < len(path)`), matching continues into `n.children[0]` (the next static segment after the param, e.g. `/edit`), via `continue walk`.
- If nothing remains, `n.handlers` is checked; if present, that's the final match and `value.fullPath = n.fullPath` is set (used later for `c.FullPath()`).

## 3. Exposing it to user code

Back in `gin.go`'s `handleHTTPRequest`, `value.params` becomes `c.Params` (a `Params` = `[]Param` slice), which `context.go`'s `(c *Context) Param(key string)` / `Params.ByName` look up linearly by key — there's no further tree involved at that point, just a slice scan.

**Catch-all (`*filepath`) params** work almost identically but use `case catchAll:` in the same switch — there, `val := path` (the entire remainder, no `/`-boundary stop), and the key is `n.path[2:]` (stripping the two-char `/*` sentinel gin stores for catch-all nodes).

Not verified: I didn't trace `context.go`'s `Param`/`MustGet`-style accessors line-by-line — inferred their behavior (linear scan over `Params`) from the `Params.Get`/`ByName` definitions already shown in tree.go rather than reading `context.go` directly.
